Report Description*****NOAA/NESDIS MPSR ISSUED FOR: GULF OF AMERICA***** POSSIBLE, UNCONFIRMED OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. REPORT DATE: 08-17-2026 REPORT TIME: 1146 UTC REGION: GULF OF AMERICA SUB REGION: N/A AREA/BLOCK: MAIN PASS 62 IMAGE DATE: 08-16-2026 IMAGE TIME: 2353 UTC DATA SOURCE: SENTINEL1D MODE: INTERFEROMETRIC WIDE (IW) VV RESOLUTION: 5X20 METER LOCATION: 29°19'22" N/88°55'47" W AREA: 26.75 SQUARE KILOMETERS CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM-HIGH REPORT MAP/GIS FILES: HTTPS://WWW.OSPO.NOAA.GOV/PRODUCTS/OCEAN/MARINEPOLLUTION/ REMARKS: POSSIBLE OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THIS ANOMALY IS UNCONFIRMED AS OIL. POSSIBLE OIL APPEARED TO DRIFT NE FROM AN UNKNOWN SOURCE IN THE MAIN PASS AREA OF LOUISIANA. THE ANOMALY HAD SHARP EDGES IN PART, AND HIGH CONTRAST AGAINST MOST OF THE SURROUNDING ENVIRONMENT. THE ANOMALY SPANNED AN AREA OF 12 NM FROM SW TO NE, AND 10 NM FROM N TO S. IT WAS BROKEN UP INTO MANY MOTTLED SEGMENTS. A POSSIBLY RELATED NOAA NESDIS RESPONSELINK MPSR WITH SIMILAR SIGNATURES WAS REPORTED IN THE AREA 8/14 (NRC 1470720). WINDS WERE 3-5 KTS FROM SSE. UNCERTAINTIES: THE EXTENT DESCRIBED IS A BEST ESTIMATE AS THERE WERE MANY FALSE POSITIVES IN THE AREA THAT BECAME MIXED WITH WHAT APPEARED TO BE OIL SIGNATURES. THE EXTENT WAS ALSO LIMITED BY THE IMAGE FOOTPRINT, NO DATA WAS AVAILABLE TO THE WEST WHERE THE OIL SIGNATURES WERE LIKELY ALSO PRESENT. WHILE NO SOURCE COULD BE IDENTIFIED, GIVEN THE RECENT AND SIMILAR REPORT, CONFIDENCE WAS MEDIUM-HIGH. IF YOU WOULD LIKE TO SHARE ANY FEEDBACK ABOUT THIS REPORT OR HAVE QUESTIONS, PLEASE CONTACT THE OPERATIONAL ANALYST AT (301) 683-1403 OR SEND TO OCEANMAP@NOAA.GOV. EMAIL ALERTS ARE AVAILABLE ONLY FOR FEDERAL AND STATE GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS INVOLVED IN RESPONSE EFFORTS. REQUESTS TO BE ADDED TO THE EMAIL ALERTS SHOULD ALSO BE SENT TO OCEANMAP@NOAA.GOV. PLEASE ALLOW UP TO 2 BUSINESS DAYS TO PROCESS THE REQUEST.

Lat/Long: 40.735657, -74.172367 (Approximated from CITY_STATE)
Report DescriptionFEB 24, 2019; MASTER MAERSK KINLOSS SENT AN EMAIL AT 2102 HOURS STATING VARIOUS CREW HAVE REPORTED SUSPICIONS OF A VIRUS(S) ON TWO ENDPOINTS THAT ARE A PART OF THE SHIPBOARD IT NETWORK; DECK OFFICE AND CONFERENCE ROOM ENDPOINTS. DESCRIBED SYMPTOMS AS SLOW PERFORMANCE AND THE CONTENTS OF USB DRIVES BEING REMOVED WHENEVER INSERTED INTO USB PORTS. FEB 25, 2019; REMOTELY BOTH ENDPOINTS WERE CLEANED, REMOVING ALL VIRUS(S)/TROJAN(S). IT WAS ALSO NOTED THAT BOTH SYSTEMS WERE WITHOUT PREVIOUSLY INSTALLED ANTIVIRUS, THIS WAS CORRECTED BY INSTALLING SAME. FEB 26, 2019; REMOTELY BOTH ENDPOINTS WERE RECHECKED TO ENSURE THE ANTIVIRUS REMAINED AS WELL AS TO RESCAN FOR VIRUSES. AGAIN IT WAS FOUND THAT THE ANTIVIRUS HAD BEEN REMOVED AND BOTH SYSTEMS WERE INFECTED AGAIN WITH A VIRUS/TROJAN. AT THIS TIME THE SERVER WAS SCANNED AND FOUND TO BE INFECTED THE SAME AS THE OTHER TWO ENDPOINTS. AT THIS TIME IT WAS AGREED THAT THE SERVER WOULD BE SCRUBBED FIRST AND ONCE CLEAN WE WOULD DO THE SAME FOR THE TWO CLIENT SYSTEMS. USING SEVERAL MALWARE REMOVAL UTILITIES INCLUDING TDSSKILLER (KASPERSKY PRODUCT) IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE NETWORKED ENDPOINTS/SERVER KEPT INFECTING EACH OTHER AFTER THEY WERE SCANNED/CLEANED. - IT WAS DECIDED THAT ALL ENDPOINTS EXCEPT THE SERVER WOULD BE POWERED OFF, MALWARE SCAN COMPLETED, AND THEN INSTALL DELL SECURITY SUITE (WE ARE IN PROCESS OF REPLACING SOPHOS ANTIVIRUS WITH DELL SECURITY SUITE FLEET-WIDE), THEN POWER UP ONE ENDPOINT AT A TIME REPEATING THE PROCESS. SERVER MALWARE SCAN COMPLETED STARTED, DELL SECURITY SUITE SOFTWARE TRANSFER TO THE VESSEL VIA SATELLITE STARTED. FEB 27, 2019; INSTALLED DELL SECURITY SUITE ON SERVER AND COMPLETED SCAN. CONTINUED THE PROCESS OF MALWARE REMOVAL SCAN AND DELL INSTALLATION ONE ENDPOINT AT A TIME. FEB 28, 2019; CONTINUING MALWARE SCAN, DELL INSTALLATION AND SCAN AT ENDPOINTS. REPLACED ONE ENDPOINT DUE TO IT COMPLETELY LOSING NETWORK/INTERNET CONNECTIVITY AFTER COMPLETING SCANS. MAR 1, 2019; INSTALLATION AND SCAN COMPLETED
